name: Bolt
description: Bolt (bolt.new) is StackBlitz's browser-based AI app builder. You describe an app or website in chat and Bolt generates, runs, and lets you edit a working full-stack prototype in the browser — no local setup — using WebContainers to run Node.js entirely client-side. Tagline: "Create stunning apps & websites by chatting with AI."

writing-chat.summary: Bolt's primary interface is a chat panel: you describe what you want built or changed in plain language, and Bolt responds by writing and running the code, with the live app updating beside the conversation.

subFeatures.name: Prompt-to-App Chat
subFeatures.description: Describe an app or a change to it in a sentence or two; Bolt writes and wires up the underlying code

subFeatures.name: Iterative Refinement
subFeatures.description: Multi-turn conversation to adjust layout, copy, and behavior of the running prototype

limitations: Chat is scoped to building/editing the current project, not general-purpose conversation
Longer projects consume more of the plan's monthly token allowance per message

pricingTiers.details: Chat-based app building with a limited daily/monthly token allowance
Higher monthly token allowance for continued chat-driven building

versionHistory.changes: Public launch of the chat-to-app browser builder

research.summary: Bolt is a build tool, not a research assistant — it does not browse the web or cite sources on its own.

subFeatures.name: Not Available
subFeatures.description: Bolt focuses on generating and running code, not open-web research

limitations: No built-in web search or citation feature
Any external data must be wired in via an integration (e.g. an API) inside the generated app

file-analysis.summary: Bolt can take an uploaded image (e.g. a design screenshot or mockup) or an imported existing codebase as input and reason over it to scaffold or modify an app.

subFeatures.name: Screenshot/Design-to-Code
subFeatures.description: Upload an image of a design or reference UI and Bolt scaffolds matching layout and components

subFeatures.name: Import Existing Project
subFeatures.description: Import a GitHub repo or existing StackBlitz project so Bolt can read and modify the current codebase

limitations: Analysis is scoped to what's uploaded or imported into the current project
Very large existing codebases may exceed practical context for a single change

pricingTiers.details: Image upload and project import within the free token allowance
Higher token allowance for larger imported projects

document-creation.summary: Bolt generates application code and content within that app (copy, sample data), not standalone documents like PDFs or slide decks.

subFeatures.name: In-App Content Only
subFeatures.description: Text/content Bolt writes lives inside the generated app's UI, not as an exportable document

limitations: No PDF, DOCX, or presentation generation
Not a general-purpose writing/document tool

pricingTiers.details: Not available as a standalone feature

image-generation.summary: Bolt does not generate images. It builds application code, and any imagery in a generated app is either uploaded by the user or placeholder content.

subFeatures.name: Not Available
subFeatures.description: No built-in image generation model or feature

limitations: No image generation capability
Real imagery must be supplied by the user or sourced from a connected asset/API

prototyping.summary: Prototyping is Bolt's defining capability: it generates a full-stack app from a natural-language description, runs it live in the browser via WebContainers, and lets you keep iterating and deploying without any local setup. This is the core of "vibe coding."

subFeatures.name: In-Browser Live Preview
subFeatures.description: Generated apps run instantly in the browser (Node.js via WebContainers) — no local install or terminal required

subFeatures.name: Full-Stack Scaffolding
subFeatures.description: Generates frontend, backend, and database wiring (e.g. via a connected Supabase project) from a plain-language description

subFeatures.name: One-Click Deploy
subFeatures.description: Deploy the running prototype to the web (e.g. via Netlify) directly from the Bolt interface

limitations: In-browser execution has resource/runtime limits compared to a full local dev environment
Larger or highly custom apps may need manual code cleanup after generation
Deploy/export destinations are limited to Bolt's supported integrations

pricingTiers.details: Prompt-to-app building, live preview, and deploy with a limited daily/monthly token allowance
Higher token allowance for larger or longer-running builds
Shared token pool and collaboration for multiple builders

versionHistory.changes: Chat-to-full-stack-app builder with in-browser WebContainers execution launched publicly

personalization.summary: Bolt does not offer persona or instruction-file style personalization of the assistant itself — each project's behavior is shaped by the prompts and code within that project, not by account-level customization.

subFeatures.name: Per-Project Only
subFeatures.description: Any "customization" lives in the generated project's own code and configuration, not in assistant-wide settings

limitations: No account-level custom instructions or persona settings
No cross-project preference memory

persistent-context.summary: Each Bolt project keeps its own chat history and generated codebase, so you can leave a project and come back to continue iterating with the prior context intact.

subFeatures.name: Per-Project History
subFeatures.description: Chat history and generated code for a project are saved and available on return

subFeatures.name: Project Dashboard
subFeatures.description: All of a user's projects are listed and reopenable from a personal dashboard

limitations: Context is scoped to a single project, not shared across projects
No cross-session memory outside a project's own history

pricingTiers.details: Same persistence with a larger token allowance for continued work

versionHistory.changes: Per-project history and dashboard included from launch

agents.summary: Bolt acts agentically within a project: it plans the changes needed, writes and runs the code, and automatically detects and fixes errors that appear in the live preview, iterating without the user hand-holding every step.

subFeatures.name: Autonomous Build Loop
subFeatures.description: Plans multi-file changes, writes code, and runs it in the live preview from a single natural-language request

subFeatures.name: Automatic Error Detection and Fixing
subFeatures.description: Detects build/runtime errors in the live preview and attempts fixes without a separate prompt

limitations: Agentic loop operates within the current project's scope, not across unrelated projects
Complex bugs may still need a manually written follow-up prompt

pricingTiers.details: Agentic build-and-fix loop within the free token allowance
Higher token allowance for longer agentic sessions

versionHistory.changes: Agentic build-and-autofix loop included from launch

connectors.summary: Bolt connects generated projects to common developer services — a database/backend (Supabase), version control (GitHub), and hosting (Netlify) — plus importing designs from Figma.

subFeatures.name: Supabase Integration
subFeatures.description: Wire a generated app to a Supabase project for database, auth, and backend functionality

subFeatures.name: GitHub Import/Export
subFeatures.description: Import an existing repo to work on, or push a generated project out to GitHub

subFeatures.name: Figma Import
subFeatures.description: Import a Figma design as the starting point for a generated app's UI

limitations: Connector set is limited to Bolt's supported integrations, not arbitrary third-party APIs out of the box
Each integration requires its own account/credentials to be connected

pricingTiers.details: Supabase, GitHub, and Figma integrations available within the free token allowance
Same integrations with a higher token allowance

versionHistory.changes: Supabase, GitHub, and Figma integrations included from launch

dictation.summary: Bolt's interface is text-based chat; it does not offer voice input or dictation.

subFeatures.name: Not Available
subFeatures.description: No voice input — prompts are typed into the chat panel

limitations: No voice input or dictation support
Browser-based interface is text-only
